 Former Tennessee Football Head Coach Butch Jones Fired in Sixth Year Leading New School
 By 
 Ryan Sylvia 
 - 
 Nov 16, 2026 
 Photo via Arkansas State Athletics 
 Former Tennessee football head coach Butch Jones has been fired as the head coach of Arkansas State, according to a report from On3. Jones was in his sixth year leading the program, but a 4-6 (2-4 Sun Belt) start through 10 games was enough for the administration to pull the plug and look elsewhere for leadership.
 Jones began his tenure at Arkansas State in 2021, ironically, the same year current Vols head coach Josh Heupel took over the Vols program. He has an overall record of 30-43 (18-28) leading the Red Wolves.
 His best season was in 2024, in which Arkansas State won eight games, including the 68 Ventures Bowl. He made three bowl games during his time, going 2-1. He won the 68 Ventures Bowl in 2024 and the Xbox Bowl in 2025, but lost the Camellia Bowl in 2023.
 The final game of the Jones Era at Arkansas State was ultimately a 28-21 loss at Coastal Carolina this past Saturday. That was the second straight loss after falling to UL Monroe the week prior and beating Georgia State, something his UT successor Jeremy Pruitt couldn’t do, at home as his final win the week before that.
 Advertisement 
 More From RTI:  Everything LSU Football HC Lane Kiffin Said to Preview Return to Tennessee, Neyland Stadium 
 Jones was the head coach at Tennessee from 2013-17. He went 9-4 in both 2015 and 2016, but was 4-6 (0-6 SEC) in 2017 before being fired and replaced by Pruitt. Prior to his time in Knoxville, Jones was the head coach at Cincinnati and Central Michigan.
 Since Jones’ tenure in Knoxville, Tennessee suffered through three rough years under Pruitt before firing him with cause due to recruiting violations. UT hired a new athletic director in Danny White, who brought along Josh Heupel with him from UCF to be the head coach of the football team after a nationwide search.
 Advertisement 
 So far, Heupel has steered Tennessee to a 53-22 (29-18 SEC) record in his time as head coach. Currently, the Vols are 8-2 (5-2) and in the playoff picture.
